title: Flaky rate-limit test exposes a fixed-window limiter that lets a burst through at every second boundary
measures: Sees that the test fails when its ten 20 ms-spaced calls straddle a clock second, because the shared limiter counts per clock-aligned bucket (Math.floor(now / windowMs)) while the README promises at most 10 requests in any rolling second, and replaces it with a rolling window in src/limits/rate-limiter.js (which also fixes the login guard, where 5 attempts before a 15-minute boundary and 5 after it double the brute-force budget). Shallow fixes pin or align the clock inside the test, add a retry or sleep, loosen the 429 assertion, or anchor the window at the first request (which passes the test but still resets the whole budget at once).
prompt: The test 'allows 10 requests per second per key and rejects the 11th' in test/rate-limiter.test.js is flaky: it fails roughly 1 run in 5, mostly on CI, with `expected 429, got 200`. Can you make it stop flaking? Please don't just skip it.

commits.message: feat(api): partner catalogue API, back-office login guard and shared rate limiter
